source.name: CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early. milestone checklists (2022 revision, AAP-endorsed)
source.note: Each milestone is something ~75% of children do by the listed age. CDC 'Movement/Physical' is split here into gross_motor and fine_motor; some CDC cognitive/social items involving hand use are placed under fine_motor.

categories.label: Other (practical life, routines, sensory, nature, music, reading)

milestones.text: Holds head up when on tummy
Moves both arms and both legs
Holds head steady without support when held
Pushes up onto elbows/forearms when on tummy
Rolls from tummy to back
Pushes up with straight arms when on tummy
Leans on hands to support self when sitting
Gets to a sitting position by self
Sits without support
Pulls up to stand
Walks holding on to furniture (cruising)
Takes a few steps on own
Walks without holding on to anyone or anything
Climbs on and off a couch or chair without help
Kicks a ball
Runs
Walks (not climbs) up a few stairs with or without help
Jumps off the ground with both feet
Opens hands briefly
Holds a toy when you put it in their hand
Uses arm to swing at toys
Brings hands to mouth
Reaches to grab a toy they want
Moves things from one hand to the other
Uses fingers to rake food toward self
Picks things up between thumb and pointer finger (pincer grasp)
Drinks from a cup without a lid, as you hold it
Uses fingers to feed self
Stacks at least two small objects
Scribbles
Tries to use a spoon
Drinks from a cup without a lid; may spill
Eats with a spoon
Holds something in one hand while using the other (e.g. holds container, takes lid off)
Uses hands to twist things (doorknobs, lids)
Turns book pages one at a time
Takes some clothes off by self
Strings items together (large beads, macaroni)
Uses a fork
Puts on some clothes by self (loose pants, jacket)
Draws a circle when shown how
Makes sounds other than crying
Reacts to loud sounds
Makes cooing sounds ("oooo", "aahh")
Makes sounds back when you talk to them
Turns head toward the sound of your voice
Takes turns making sounds with you
Blows raspberries
Makes squealing noises
Makes many different sounds like "mamamama" and "babababa"
Lifts arms up to be picked up
Waves bye-bye
Calls a parent "mama", "dada", or another special name
Understands "no" (pauses briefly or stops)
Tries to say one or two words besides mama/dada
Looks at a familiar object when you name it
Follows directions given with both a gesture and words
Points to ask for something or to get help
Tries to say three or more words besides mama/dada
Follows one-step directions without gestures
Points to things in a book when you ask
Says at least two words together ("more milk")
Points to at least two body parts when asked
Uses gestures beyond waving and pointing (blowing a kiss, nodding yes)
Says about 50 words
Says two or more words with one action word ("doggie run")
Names things in a book when you point and ask
Says words like "I", "me", or "we"
Talks with you in conversation using at least two back-and-forth exchanges
Asks who, what, where, or why questions
Says what action is happening in a picture or book when asked
Says first name when asked
Talks well enough for others to understand, most of the time
Calms down when spoken to or picked up
Looks at your face
Seems happy to see you when you walk up
Smiles when you talk to or smile at them
Smiles on their own to get your attention
Chuckles when you try to make them laugh
Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to get or keep your attention
Knows familiar people
Likes to look at self in a mirror
Laughs
Is shy, clingy, or fearful around strangers
Shows several facial expressions (happy, sad, angry, surprised)
Looks when you call their name
Reacts when you leave (looks, reaches for you, or cries)
Smiles or laughs when you play peek-a-boo
Plays games with you, like pat-a-cake
Copies other children while playing
Shows you an object they like
Claps when excited
Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
Shows you affection (hugs, cuddles, kisses)
Moves away from you but looks to make sure you are close by
Points to show you something interesting
Puts hands out for you to wash them
Looks at a few pages in a book with you
Helps you dress them by pushing arm through sleeve or lifting foot
Notices when others are hurt or upset
Looks at your face to see how to react in a new situation
Plays next to other children and sometimes plays with them
Shows you what they can do ("Look at me!")
Follows simple routines when told (helps pick up toys)
Calms down within 10 minutes after you leave (e.g. childcare drop-off)
Notices other children and joins them to play
Watches you as you move
Looks at a toy for several seconds
If hungry, opens mouth when they see breast or bottle
Looks at own hands with interest
Puts things in mouth to explore them
Closes lips to show they don't want more food
Looks for objects when dropped out of sight
Bangs two things together
Puts something in a container
Looks for things they see you hide
Tries to use things the right way (phone, cup, book)
Copies you doing chores, like sweeping
Plays with toys in a simple way, like pushing a toy car
Tries to use switches, knobs, or buttons on a toy
Plays with more than one toy at the same time
Uses things to pretend (feeds a block to a doll as if it were food)
Shows simple problem-solving, like standing on a small stool to reach something
Follows two-step instructions
Shows they know at least one color
Avoids touching hot objects when warned
